correctness.rationale: The given planar random-polytope input functionals I_A∝∫κρ^-2 ds and I_P∝∫κ²ρ^-2 ds, with E=a²sin²θ+b²cos²θ, ds=sqrt(E)dθ and κ=ab E^-3/2, transform exactly to <q^-2> and <Wq^-2> after separate normalization. Hölder gives inf_{<q>=1}<Fq^-2>=<F^(1/3)>³ with unique q proportional to F^(1/3). Fλ=λ+(1-λ)W, Hλ=<Fλ^(1/3)> is strictly concave for noncircular ellipse, satisfies H(0)=H(1)=1 and has unique interior λ*, H'(λ*)=0. q*=Fλ*^(1/3)/Hλ* balances R_A and R_P and attains the minimax lower bound, unique by Hölder. Uniform Taylor E=1-2epsilon cos2θ+epsilon² gives Hλ=1+λ(1−λ)epsilon²/2+O(epsilon³), hence M=1+3epsilon²/8+O(epsilon³); circle q=1. Independent angular quadrature/bisection at ε=.01,.1,.5,.95 reproduced equal objectives and near-circle coefficient .375014 at ε=.01. Continuous proof, not quadrature, proves all eccentricities.
